stories.title: Canada’s next budget to be unveiled Thursday with affordability, tax and investment measures
stories.summary: The federal budget, to be presented on Thursday, will contain new affordability measures, business tax incentives and spending on infrastructure, defence and culture, a senior government source said. It will also give further detail on private investment in Canada’s four largest airports, the government’s plan to balance the operational budget a year early, foreign direct investment flows, and an update on the Canada Strong Fund. Finance Minister François‑Philippe Champagne has already posted the budget’s title and cover on social media.
stories.why: The budget outlines fiscal priorities that will affect Canadians’ cost of living, business environment and national infrastructure development.

stories.title: Anthropic reports third-quarter revenue near $17 billion, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier
stories.summary: Anthropic disclosed in an amended IPO filing that its third‑quarter revenue was almost $17 billion, a sharp increase from $1.4 billion in the same quarter a year earlier. The filing provides the first detailed financials as the company prepares for a potential IPO. Sources cited are CNBC and Reuters.
stories.why: The figures give investors concrete data to evaluate Anthropic’s valuation ahead of its planned stock market debut.

stories.title: US to remove South Africa and Rwanda from AGOA in 2027
stories.summary: The Trump administration has notified Congress that it intends to withdraw South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) preferential trade programme, effective 1 January 2027. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said an annual review found both countries were engaging in practices inconsistent with AGOA eligibility, and the two nations have been formally notified of the decision.
stories.why: The removal will end duty‑free access for many African exports to the United States, potentially reducing trade volumes and harming the economies of the affected countries.

stories.title: Omen AI acquires Aquatic Labs for $16 million
stories.summary: Omen AI, founded in 2024 to monitor cooling water in data‑center chips, announced a $16 million cash‑and‑stock acquisition of competitor Aquatic Labs. The deal follows Omen’s $31 million Series A round raised in June and combines Omen’s element‑detection sensors with Aquatic Labs’ alkalinity‑testing technology to provide a richer real‑time view of cooling fluids.
stories.why: The combined sensor can improve water‑use monitoring, potentially reducing consumption and operational costs in AI data centers.
stories.previousTitle: Omen AI adds liquid know-how in $16 million Aquatic Labs acquisition
stories.previousSummary: After raising a $31 million Series A in June, Omen is now acquiring competitor Aquatic Labs in a $16 million cash-and-stock deal. The deal came together after Omen founder Zach Laberge was introduced to Aquatic Labs’ CEO Allan Adams by an investor in the filtration space.
